recognize_zh: 周邊血液兩顆中型淋巴球：核圓、染色質中度凝集（比母細胞粗），細胞質中等量淡藍；下方細胞核中央可見一個核仁輪廓，這種「成熟染色質＋明顯單一核仁」的組合是前淋巴球（prolymphocyte）的線索。
features: Two medium-sized lymphoid cells, roughly twice the diameter of a small lymphocyte
Round nuclei with moderately condensed chromatin, coarser than blast chromatin
Single central nucleolus suggested in the lower cell
Moderate rim of pale blue cytoplasm
Background red cells with rouleaux-like stacking in thicker areas
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows two medium-sized lymphoid cells with round nuclei, moderately condensed chromatin and a moderate rim of pale blue cytoplasm; the lower cell shows a single central nucleolus. The chromatin is more mature than that of lymphoblasts. Findings are suggestive of prolymphocytes; in context of a marked lymphocytosis with more than 55% such cells this would suggest prolymphocytic leukemia, although B-PLL is no longer a distinct entity in WHO 2022 and cases are reclassified (e.g., as mantle cell lymphoma, CLL in progression or splenic B-cell lymphoma with prominent nucleoli). Flow cytometry and cyclin D1/CCND1 testing are required.

ddx.vs: Lymphoblasts have finely dispersed chromatin and scant cytoplasm and are TdT/CD34-positive, whereas these cells have condensed chromatin with a distinct nucleolus.

ddx.dx: Mantle cell lymphoma, blastoid or leukemic
ddx.vs: Can look identical; cyclin D1 expression or t(11;14) identifies mantle cell lymphoma.
Prolymphocytes are admixed with a background of small mature CLL cells and smudge cells, with a CD5+/CD23+ dim-sIg phenotype.
T-PLL cells are smaller with irregular nuclear outlines and cytoplasmic blebs and express T-cell markers with TCL1A rearrangement.
